dedupe_keys.name: doe building energy codes program state energy code adoption status and analysis

description: The DOE Building Energy Codes Program tracks each state's adoption of energy codes for residential and commercial buildings, reviewed against the national model codes, the International Energy Conservation Code (IECC) for residential buildings and ASHRAE Standard 90.1 for commercial buildings, as required by 42 USC 6833. Equivalence is now assessed quantitatively: each state's base code and amendments are run through DOE's energy modelling framework to give an energy index, the ratio of whole-building site energy intensity to that of the 2006 IECC (residential) or 90.1-2004 (commercial), aggregated across building, foundation and system types and climate zones with weights from new construction permits; a state code whose index is not more than 1 per cent above a model code edition counts as equivalent, and PNNL may use analysis by others for codes that differ fundamentally. Coverage: US states and territories. Access: free web pages. Licence: not stated. Caveats: the index describes code stringency, not compliance or the existing stock, and local adoptions in home-rule states are not the same as state codes. Simulation uses: setting envelope and equipment assumptions for new buildings by state in stock and policy models. Related records: the ACEEE State and Local Policy Database and the State Climate Policy Dashboard.
